why: PAGE is a school-day implementation of CANONICAL’s free-choice learning principle, adding a specific setting and infrastructure pattern.
first_why: This is a school-based implementation of free-choice learning environment design, adding infrastructure and facilitation details while its evidence belongs on the broader canonical principle.

why: PAGE is a narrower professional-development component focused on mentoring and advocacy supports for implementing new instructional skills and facilitating teacher learning communities.
first_why: The mentoring cycle of planning, goal-setting, observation, and debriefing is a narrower implementation of the canonical teacher professional-development pattern of coached practice with feedback, while advocacy meetings add a collaborative-support component.

why: PAGE describes a distinct mentoring-and-sustainability stage, including coach professional development and fostering independent teacher communities, rather than merely participation in a community of practice.
first_why: The proposed level-3 practice is chiefly the reusable formation and eventual independence of teacher communities of practice, while the coaching context is only its setting and support mechanism.

why: PAGE addresses debate as a research laboratory accountable to argumentation theory, a distinct meta-theoretical purpose rather than a narrower instructional use of CANONICAL.
first_why: The candidate is a narrower theoretical account of the canonical Debate pattern, adding that debate improves argumentation only when its resolutions, evidence practices, and response rules remain accountable to argumentation principles.

why: PAGE catalogs Direct Instruction’s distinctive lesson routines, which are a specific implementation pattern not captured by CANONICAL’s general explicit-teaching sequence
first_why: The listed scripted, highly structured, guided-response, pacing, and correction routines are distinctive component practices of the canonical Direct Instruction pattern.

why: PAGE describes an expert-panel item-selection procedure, not the broader principle of validity, reliability, or bias in interpreting assessment results.
first_why: Expert review and consensus-based winnowing of assessment items is a narrower content-validity practice covered by Validity, Reliability, and Bias in Classroom Assessment.

why: PAGE offers a distinct taxonomy for evaluating prompt compliance rather than describing the plan–monitor–act SRL policy.
first_why: The taxonomy and its evidence concern how compliance with reusable self-regulated-learning prompts is observed and related to learning, making it a narrower empirical case of the Self-Regulated Learning pattern.

why: PAGE presents a distinct taxonomy of three fading approaches rather than a particular instance or restatement of the canonical principle.
first_why: The three fading-based approaches are reusable forms of contingent scaffolding and fading, so their evidence belongs on the canonical Scaffolding and Fading page.

why: PAGE presents a distinct, multi-category pattern for implicit scaffolding in simulations, broader than the affordance-and-constraint principle.
first_why: The four-category simulation pattern is a medium-specific elaboration of designing affordances, representations, feedback, and constraints so learners can use tools productively without explicit instructions.

why: refused by the second pass: PAGE presents a distinct four-quadrant learner–instructor matching framework rather than a specific case of contingent scaffolding and fading
first_why: The quadrant progression is a reusable scaffolding-and-fading pattern that calibrates instructor direction and support to learner readiness and gradually transfers control to the learner.

why: PAGE presents a broader four-part taxonomy of reflective methods, only one of which is video replay analysis.
first_why: The candidate directly elaborates video replay analysis as a way to make learner performance an object of review, while its other reflection methods are extensions of that practice.

why: PAGE describes a distinct progression from oral BICS to written CALP rather than a narrower instance of integrating cognitive challenge, academic content, and critical language awareness.
first_why: The Functional Approach is a narrower bilingual instructional progression toward CALP, so its rationale and sequencing evidence belong with the broader principle of promoting bilingual students' CALP, although that page does not fully specify the oral-to-written progression.

why: PAGE is a distinct multi-component teacher-research model, not merely a narrower statement of the general strengths-based principle.
first_why: The household inquiry and subsequent classroom innovations are a contextualized implementation of collecting evidence of learners' existing capabilities and building instruction from those strengths.

why: PAGE is a distinct equation-focused instructional sequence, not merely a narrower case of CANONICAL's general conceptual-understanding pattern
first_why: Guided Equation Appropriation is a domain-specific instance of Develop Understanding, using elicited mechanistic reasoning, guided explanation, self-explanation, and transfer checks before formal application and interpretation.

why: Guided participation is a distinct, broader account of adult-child joint activity and cultural induction, not a narrower case of cognitive apprenticeship.
first_why: Guided participation is a broader adult–learner joint-activity pattern whose bridging, communication, and movement toward independent functioning should inform the Cognitive Apprenticeship page, although it adds explicit activity and goal selection beyond that page’s current emphasis.

why: PAGE concerns the broader purposes and contextual goals of guided practice in teacher learning, not the canonical principle of scaffolded skill practice.
first_why: The candidate directly elaborates the reusable idea of guided practice by identifying its broad purposes in teacher learning, rather than proposing a distinct programme or setting-specific design.

why: Hunter’s model is a distinct, comprehensive lesson-sequencing framework with curriculum analysis and anticipatory-set elements beyond Direct Instruction’s core explanation, modeling, guided practice, and feedback pattern.
first_why: Hunter's model is a reusable teacher-led, explicit instructional sequence and therefore belongs with the canonical Direct Instruction pattern; the reported implementation finding is relevant evidence about its effectiveness.

why: PAGE is a distinct course-design pattern centered on a shared research paper and CBRE structure, not a narrower statement of CANONICAL’s conceptual, dialogic theory of interdisciplinarity.
first_why: The interdisciplinary course-based research pattern operationalizes a conceptual, dialogic approach to interdisciplinarity through a shared boundary object, though its single qualitative study provides only weak supporting evidence.

why: Jigsaw is a narrower cooperative-learning component of FCL's broader community-based pattern.
first_why: The candidate is a general jigsaw-based expert-teaching cycle, which is already covered by Fostering Communities of Learning, although several cited claims concern supporting mechanisms rather than the page's central jigsaw relationship.

why: Jigsaw is a specific cooperative-learning structure that implements positive interdependence and individual accountability.
first_why: The within-team and expert jigsaw variants are narrower reusable cooperative-learning structures that instantiate positive interdependence and individual accountability, so their evidence belongs on the canonical Cooperative Learning pattern page.

why: refused by the second pass: JiTT is a distinct feedback-loop teaching method, not merely a narrower instance of delivering support at the moment of performance.
first_why: Just-in-Time Teaching is the canonical reusable pattern for using pre-class responses to adapt instruction and devote class time to active learning.

why: Keypad quizzing is a narrower lecture-based implementation of formative assessment that elicits responses, interprets results, and enables immediate instructional action.
first_why: Keypad quizzing is a reusable formative-assessment pattern that repeatedly elicits learner evidence during instruction and enables immediate instructional response.

why: Literature Circles with rotating discussion roles are a distinct reading-specific pedagogy and do not state Collaborative Learning's required elicitation, reasoning-task, and individual-check policy.
first_why: Literature circles are a reading-specific form of collaborative learning, with peer interaction and rotating roles supplying structured joint work, although the source does not establish all of the canonical page's accountability features.

why: PAGE specifies a distinct seven-step Maastricht tutorial cycle with progressive disclosure, presentation, and feedback, which the broad PBL policy does not capture.
first_why: This is a course-level implementation of the reusable Problem-Based Learning pattern, and its claims provide weak qualitative evidence about collaboration and learning in PBL rather than constituting a distinct general pattern.

why: PAGE describes a lesson-level instance of CANONICAL's mastery-learning cycle of formative assessment, corrective support, and reassessment before progression.
first_why: The candidate describes the canonical Mastery Learning pattern of formative checks followed by corrective instruction, relearning, and reassessment before advancing.

why: PAGE presents Merrill’s broader instructional-phase corollaries, not a narrower case of Cognitive Apprenticeship.
first_why: The demonstration and application corollaries substantially elaborate Cognitive Apprenticeship's modeling, coaching, scaffolding, and fading, while integration adds a compatible transfer-and-reflection endpoint.

why: PAGE presents a broader, enumerative framework of cooperative-lesson elements rather than the specific accountability-and-individual-check policy captured by CANONICAL.
first_why: This is a reusable cooperative-learning lesson pattern whose nine elements elaborate the canonical Cooperative Learning pattern, and its cited claims belong as supporting or testing evidence for that page.

why: PAGE describes a distinct, specific open-ended role-play method with collaborative planning and debriefing, whereas CANONICAL presents a broad spectrum of practice types.
first_why: The open-ended scenario is a reusable language-teaching role-play sequence, and the canonical spectrum page directly covers communicative drills, role plays, and related practice types.

why: PAGE identifies enabling conditions for scholarly PLC inquiry, a distinct pattern rather than a narrower instance of sustained communities of practice.
first_why: The proposed PLC pattern is a more specific professional-learning application of Communities of Practice, extending its shared participation and trust-based critical inquiry with reflection, dialogue, common purpose, and accountability.

why: PAGE describes a three-phase field-trip activity schedule, not CANONICAL's repeating experience–reflection–conceptualization–experimentation learning cycle.
first_why: The reusable pre-visit/on-site/post-visit arc is a field-trip implementation of the canonical Experiential Learning Cycle, and its cited claims directly concern whether sequencing experience with preparation and follow-up improves learning.

why: PAGE states Merrill’s broader problem-centered instructional principle, whereas CANONICAL describes the narrower Problem-Based Learning model.
first_why: This is a general problem-centred instructional pattern whose whole-task engagement and progression prescriptions belong on the canonical Problem-Based Learning page, although the source supplies no empirical claims to assess.

why: PAGE is a domain-specific instance of sequencing that applies the general principle to progressive listening-skill demands.
first_why: The four-stage listening progression is a reusable sequencing pattern, and its cited claim provides weak support for placing aural-comprehension demands before oral production in an increasing-complexity sequence.

why: PAGE defines a distinct typology of mediation moves and their implicit-to-explicit ordering, without stating contingent withdrawal, fading, or independent-performance outcomes.
first_why: The typology is a medium-specific instance of scaffolding and fading, using graduated mediation matched to learners' ZPD and withdrawing or increasing support as needed.

why: PAGE is a distinct scripted, socially distributed inquiry sequence rather than a narrower case of LfU’s motivation–construction–application model.
first_why: Scripted personally meaningful inquiry is a narrower orchestration of Learning-for-Use, connecting meaningful learner-generated questions with evidence gathering, application, and revision, although the software-specific scripting is an implementation detail.

why: Socratic Seminar is a distinct discussion pattern, not a narrower case of the Community of Inquiry principle.
first_why: Socratic Seminar is a structured form of Community of Inquiry, adding text-centered preparation, facilitation, norms, and questioning to the canonical framework's shared movement toward understanding.

why: Storyline curriculum design is a distinct student-generated-question sequencing approach, not a narrower case of anchored instruction.
first_why: Storyline curriculum is a student-question-driven form of anchored instruction: an anchoring phenomenon organizes a reusable unit and makes target disciplinary ideas necessary, while its question sequence adds a distinctive implementation detail.

why: PAGE is a narrower studio-course case of CANONICAL’s teacher-as-guide-and-consultant principle.
first_why: The source directly illustrates the principle that teachers in student-centered learning should act as designers, guides, and academic consultants rather than traditional content disseminators.

why: PAGE states the whole-task sequencing and distributed tell/show/do principle that is a narrower component of CANONICAL's 4C/ID pattern.
first_why: The task-centered strategy is a whole-task sequencing pattern closely aligned with 4C/ID's progression of increasingly complex whole learning tasks with demonstrations, information, and practice distributed across the progression.

why: PAGE describes a broader three-phase language-learning practice protocol, including design, execution, and assessment, rather than merely a narrower case of the Deliberate Practice principle.
first_why: The three-phase protocol is a language-learning instantiation of deliberate practice, adding domain-specific guidance on individualized design, goal-directed repetition, feedback, and reassessment rather than constituting a distinct general pattern.

why: PAGE is a narrower task-sequencing instance of 4C/ID's whole-task progression from simple to complex while managing cognitive load.
first_why: The candidate is a narrower whole-task progression pattern within 4C/ID, using simple-to-complex task classes and limited new components to manage cognitive load and support transfer.

why: PAGE focuses on accelerated contextualized instruction and cohort support, a distinct learning mechanism rather than linking program elements to workforce entry points or credentials.
first_why: The contextualized construction curriculum links basic-skills learning to a workforce pathway and immediate purpose, although cohort support and acceleration extend beyond that page's central recommendation.

why: PAGE is a broader constructivist principle about using learners’ existing ideas, not the narrower mechanism of creating cognitive disequilibrium through mismatch or contradiction.
first_why: The candidate is a science-specific instance of conceptual change in which learners' existing explanations are confronted and replaced through instruction, although it does not directly test cognitive disequilibrium as the mechanism.

why: PAGE is a distinct principle about acknowledging asymmetrical grading and evaluative power rather than presuming equality, not merely a narrower case of CANONICAL's call for equal relations.
first_why: The source directly supports equal association and communication while adding that genuine collaboration must acknowledge faculty's evaluative power rather than assume false equality.

why: PAGE is a broader science-teaching activity pattern encompassing psychomotor and attitudinal activity, not merely CANONICAL’s meaningful cognitive work with content.
first_why: The recommendation that pupils learn through active, hands-on involvement is the canonical Active Learning principle, while the cited arrangement finding is a context-specific affordance supporting that practice.

why: PAGE is a narrower form of adaptive learning that sequences tasks using diagnosed knowledge states and prerequisite structure.
first_why: The candidate is a narrower application of adaptive learning that selects learning paths and next activities using both learner knowledge estimates and prerequisite structure, which the canonical page should cover.

why: PAGE concerns supplementing game-based training with instructional strategies broadly, not solely the narrower worked-example pattern.
first_why: The recommendation is a game-context application of the canonical worked-examples principle, and both cited findings directly test whether studying worked examples improves learning and transfer.

why: refused by the second pass: PAGE concerns adult support developing children as active agents alongside subject learning, which is broader and distinct from CANONICAL’s specific focus on autonomy as volition and self-endorsement.
first_why: The recommendation directly supports the canonical principle of cultivating learner autonomy by framing adult assistance as developing children’s agency rather than merely transmitting subject knowledge.

why: PAGE is a distinct caution about the non-transferability of sequencing principles to affective learning, not a narrower instance of CANONICAL’s general sequencing idea.
first_why: The candidate is a domain-specific qualification of the canonical sequencing principle, showing that affective learning requires sequencing dimensions and dependencies that should not be imported uncritically from other domains.

why: PAGE is a narrower ESL-classroom application of expanding adult learners’ social networks through peer support and mentoring.
first_why: The peer cooperation and mentoring described are a narrower adult-ESL instance of expanding learners' social networks and access to social support.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of CANONICAL that treats learners’ stated grammar-learning preferences as a learner variable informing instructional approach, syllabus, and materials decisions.
first_why: The candidate is a narrower language-teaching application of basing grammar decisions on learner needs and variables, with stated instructional preferences serving as one such variable.

why: PAGE adds the distinct activity-theory principle of identifying contradictions as engines of change, which CANONICAL does not state.
first_why: The recommendation to analyze whole activity systems and use their contradictions to guide redesign is a direct, more specific application of the canonical principle of systemic understanding in change efforts.

why: PAGE describes a narrower application of formative assessment in which student dialogue turns are used to infer learner progress and guide feedback.
first_why: The candidate specifies a reusable formative-assessment practice—analyzing student dialogue turns to diagnose progress and misconceptions—rather than introducing a distinct general principle.

why: PAGE presents a distinct teacher-development mechanism for appropriating authentic disciplinary practice to challenge exclusionary narratives, not merely a narrower case of helping students view disciplines as modes of inquiry.
first_why: The candidate directly supports teaching disciplinary tools as situated modes of inquiry rather than fixed procedures, while its single qualitative case provides only weak illustrative evidence.

why: PAGE is a narrower instructional application of Sequencing, specifying progressive articulation of the definite integral’s partial meanings.
first_why: The candidate is a calculus-specific application of sequencing: progressively ordering and articulating related meanings so later understanding builds on an organized network of prior knowledge.

why: PAGE is a narrower, learner-directed personalization case in which an individual child's preferences guide AAC-system selection.
first_why: The recommendation to assess each child's preferences and use them to individualize AAC selection is a domain-specific application of Personalization, whereas the cited preference difference only supports the need for individualization.

why: PAGE concerns assessing listening differences between learner groups to inform course design, not adapting instruction in real time to emerging student thinking.
first_why: The recommendation is a language-specific instance of responsive teaching: assess learners' differing needs, perceptions, strategies, and performance before adapting pedagogy, rather than relying on heritage-status assumptions.

why: PAGE is a narrower assessment principle for fostering creative thinking, focused on prioritizing learners’ processes over products in maker education.
first_why: The recommendation to focus assessment on process rather than products is a narrower application of protecting creative thinking and intrinsic motivation from constant evaluation.

why: PAGE is a financial-education-specific application of the broader spaced-learning principle.
first_why: The candidate is a narrower financial-education application of the canonical Spaced Learning principle, with retrieval practice as the activity distributed across delayed intervals.

why: refused by the second pass: PAGE treats autonomy as active meaning-making and literacy practice in early literacy, a distinct pedagogical conception from CANONICAL's motivational autonomy through choice and non-controlling support.
first_why: The candidate generalizes learner autonomy as both a design means and an educational end, so its early-literacy case and qualification belong on the canonical Autonomy page.

why: PAGE presents a distinct principle of balancing challenge and support for novice library users, not contingent support that is gradually withdrawn as competence develops.
first_why: The recommendation is a general case of scaffolding and fading, in which calibrated support and challenge help novices progress toward independence rather than dependence or abandonment.

why: PAGE states a narrower condition of the Retrieval Practice principle, explaining how retrieval support and effort affect its effectiveness.
first_why: The chapter provides a directly relevant qualification of retrieval practice: reduce support to increase effort while preserving successful or feedback-corrected retrieval, and its evidence belongs on the canonical Retrieval Practice page.

why: PAGE addresses balancing goal guidance with creator freedom in level editors, whereas CANONICAL concerns guaranteeing productive tool use through affordances and constraints without instructions.
first_why: The candidate directly applies the canonical principle that tools should use affordances and constraints to guide productive use, while adding a motivation-sensitive limit on restrictiveness.

why: PAGE is a narrower formal-education application of character education focused on developing civic virtues and competence.
first_why: The candidate presents character education as a general approach for developing moral, civic, intellectual, and performative virtues, directly matching the canonical Character Education principle.

why: PAGE presents a broader principle of advocacy, purposeful change, and ongoing professional growth, not the specific claim that professional development should use study teams and peer coaching.
first_why: The candidate directly supports the canonical principle that teacher professional development should be ongoing, collaborative, and embedded in coaching and professional learning rather than evaluative or limited to one-off events.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of CANONICAL’s principle of balancing competing teaching methods, specifically combining communicative and traditional approaches.
first_why: The candidate restates the canonical principle of balancing competing educational approaches rather than adopting one method exclusively.

why: PAGE gives a narrower information-literacy application of CANONICAL’s principle by combining problem-based and simulation methods according to their respective affordances.
first_why: The candidate is a domain-specific application of harmonizing competing instructional approaches by selecting each method for the affordance it serves, although the comparative study does not directly test their integrated use.

why: PAGE is a narrower multimedia-learning application of making structure and important changes visible through signalling and visual cues
first_why: The recommendation is a multimedia-specific instance of making important structure or changes explicit through signals and visual cues, while its findings provide weak, condition-dependent evidence about attention and detection rather than learning outcomes.

why: PAGE focuses on making language input comprehensible through proficiency-adjusted delivery, not on temporary support that enables performance beyond independent ability.
first_why: Adjusting explanations, representations, delivery, and task demands to learners' proficiency is a general form of scaffolding for making communicative input comprehensible, although the page may not foreground language instruction.

why: PAGE makes a broader universal-benefit claim about adapting training for NESB workers, not specifically the vocabulary-and-syntax principle in CANONICAL.
first_why: The source supports Accessible Vocabulary & Syntax by arguing that clear, comprehensible language removes avoidable barriers for language-minority workers and improves training for everyone.

why: PAGE specifies composition criteria for peer-teaching flipped-classroom groups and roles, not the adaptive, evidence-based re-forming that defines CANONICAL.
first_why: The recommendation is a setting-specific application of flexible grouping, using learner-background and prior-achievement evidence to form groups and assign roles, although the study does not directly test flexible regrouping itself.

why: PAGE combines a narrower contextualization claim with distinct guidance on visual vocabulary teaching, reduced distractions, and predictable routines.
first_why: The candidate's central recommendation is to connect abstract instruction to learners' familiar biographical, family, and daily-life experiences, while the visual and embodied vocabulary supports are a contextualized implementation detail.

why: PAGE describes a curriculum-structured form of personalization that adapts each learner’s pace and instruction without requiring one-to-one teaching.
first_why: The candidate recommends personalizing curriculum structure, pacing, and instructional arrangements to individual learner needs, which is the central idea of Personalization.

why: PAGE presents a broader service continuum and teacher-development recommendation, whereas CANONICAL focuses on mastery-based acceleration or enrichment.
first_why: The recommendation directly concerns supporting gifted and talented students through differentiated instruction, enrichment, acceleration, advanced provision, and teacher capability, while broadening the canonical page's response-based guidance.

why: PAGE is a distinct principle about deliberately creating social interaction for meaning to arise, not merely organizing education around the child's response to provided material.
first_why: The candidate directly extends the canonical principle's Mead-based emphasis on organizing education around the learner's own response, specifying that social situations should elicit that response and meaning-making.

why: PAGE is a distinct principle about critiquing humanist epistemologies and the politics of Anthropocene historicization, not a narrower case of CANONICAL's more-than-human and anti-anthropocentric concern.
first_why: The candidate is a language-and-history-focused application of the canonical principle that critical communication pedagogy must challenge anthropocentrism and extend concern beyond the human.

why: PAGE states a cross-curricular multimedia-production sequence that is a direct, narrower formulation of CANONICAL's learning-by-producing pattern.
first_why: The proposed cross-curricular unit is a reusable multimedia-production learning sequence and its evidence belongs on the canonical Learning by Producing page.

why: PAGE is an adult-education-specific application of CANONICAL’s principle of treating learners’ cultural knowledge and experiences as curriculum assets to support inclusion and engagement.
first_why: The recommendation is a direct instance of connecting curriculum and discussion to learners' cultural and life experiences, and is broadly reusable beyond adult education.

why: PAGE presents a broader set of curriculum-embedded, teacher-led, sustained professional-development principles rather than CANONICAL's specific emphasis on study teams and peer coaching.
first_why: The candidate's curriculum-embedded, teacher-led, sustained, collaborative professional development is a broader instance of the canonical recommendation to use ongoing professional learning activities such as study teams and peer coaching rather than one-off sessions.

why: PAGE concerns course-level flexibility and coach-enabled responsiveness to unanticipated needs, not the narrower instructional practice of adapting in real time to evidence of student thinking.
first_why: The recommendation is a course-level implementation of responsive teaching, using curricular flexibility and coach improvisation to adapt instruction to learners' emerging needs, though it is not specifically emergent curriculum built from student interests.

why: PAGE is a narrower asynchronous-learning application of Feedback Loops, focusing on formative feedback applied to reviewable external outputs to prompt higher engagement.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower asynchronous application of closing feedback loops by making learner outputs observable and using formative information to support subsequent higher-level activity.

why: PAGE is a narrower, prior-knowledge-dependent case of calibrating presentation and support to learner expertise to manage cognitive load
first_why: The source directly qualifies cognitive load management by showing that instructional design revisions can reduce or increase learners' processing demands depending on prior knowledge, a condition the canonical page should include.

why: PAGE combines student direction with public and social task design, so it is a distinct engagement principle rather than a narrower case of Autonomy.
first_why: The candidate generalizes the autonomy principle by recommending meaningful student control and ownership through student-directed, socially structured online tasks, although its public peer interaction also supports social presence.

why: PAGE advocates interviewing actual curriculum users generally, whereas CANONICAL specifically concerns co-creating environments with students from groups experiencing inequities.
first_why: The candidate directly supports co-creating learning environments with marginalized students rather than designing for imagined users, although it emphasizes empathy interviews as the participation method.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of cognitive load management that calibrates instructional design to a topic’s element interactivity and resulting working-memory demands.
first_why: The recommendation is a direct application of cognitive-load management: diagnose element interactivity and adapt instructional design to manage learners' working-memory demands.

why: PAGE presents a distinct safe-dialogue principle in film education rather than the Community of Inquiry framework's interaction of social, cognitive, and teaching presence
first_why: The candidate's general recommendation that learners construct understanding through open, perspective-taking dialogue in a safe environment belongs on the broader Community of Inquiry page, while its film context is only a narrower application.

why: PAGE is a vocabulary-materials application of UDL's broader principle of offering multiple routes to accommodate learner variability.
first_why: Offering varied exercise types is a vocabulary-specific implementation of Universal Design for Learning's recommendation to provide multiple routes into learning for learner variability.

why: PAGE advocates broader ongoing learning through feedback, self-assessment, reflection, and revision, without requiring CANONICAL's closed cycle of performance-based adjustment and rechecking.
first_why: The proposed cycle of regular feedback, self-assessment, revision, and adjustment is a language-instruction instance of closing feedback loops, although the claim provides only indirect support for that central relationship.

why: PAGE is a broader claim about teacher development and collaboration sustaining DL2F implementation, while CANONICAL specifies particular professional-development activities and adult-learning practices.
first_why: The candidate's recommendation that professional development be ongoing and sustained, with collaborative educator practices, is a broader or narrower case of the canonical principle favoring continuing study teams and peer coaching over one-off sessions.

why: PAGE is a communicative-language-teaching case of the broader principle that educators facilitate learning rather than act as authoritarian content disseminators.
first_why: The source directly supports educators acting as facilitators who guide active learners rather than relying on authoritarian, content-disseminating instruction, while its dual-role language adds a language-learning context.

why: PAGE addresses eliminating a distinct guessing-based instructional practice, not a narrower case of the phonics principle.
first_why: The recommendation to replace three-cueing with sounding out is a specific curricular application of the canonical Phonics principle, though its policy assertion supplies weak evidence.

why: PAGE specifically asserts Indigenous authority over teaching and formal recognition of community expertise, which is a distinct principle rather than a narrower case of co-creating educational systems.
first_why: The recommendation is a culturally specific application of shared power in which an excluded community retains authority over how its knowledge is taught and is formally recognised as an educational partner.

why: refused by the second pass: PAGE's central idea is the sequencing of communicative interaction before corrective focus on form, which is distinct from CANONICAL's broader claim about using dialogue as a means of learning.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower writing-based application of using dialogue and student-centered communication as the means for learning, while its staged focus on form is an implementation detail.

why: PAGE concerns centering instructional planning on SEP-mandated expected learnings, whereas CANONICAL concerns deriving content from competencies.
first_why: The candidate generalizes the principle that planning should begin from competency-linked expected learnings and let teachers select content, strategies, and resources afterward.

why: PAGE is a narrower course-design application of CANONICAL’s experiential-learning principle, specifying practice, reflection on practice, feedback, and guided further attempts.
first_why: The recommendation is a practice-centred application of the canonical experiential-learning principle that experience, reflection, and further supported attempts build applied capability.

why: PAGE presents a distinct program-level curriculum implementation principle, whereas CANONICAL describes the general experiential learning process and its elements.
first_why: The recommendation is a program-level implementation of experiential learning, and the canonical page covers experiential learning as a reusable practice while this source adds evidence that coherence across a curriculum matters.

why: PAGE advocates explicit morphological instruction as a curriculum-wide component for EFL secondary learners, which is distinct from CANONICAL’s targeted explicit teaching and repeated practice of selected vocabulary.
first_why: Explicit morphology instruction is a vocabulary-focused form of explicit instruction, although this source adds morphological awareness and curriculum-integration details not central to the canonical page.

why: PAGE is a domain-specific curriculum recommendation about reading-strategy instruction and learner needs, not the full direct-instruction pattern of modeling, guided practice, checks, and handover.
first_why: The candidate is a content-specific application of the canonical Direct Instruction pattern: explicitly explain and model reading-comprehension strategies, guide practice, and support independent use.

why: PAGE is a narrower professional-development application of the canonical strengths-based principle, focused on teachers’ existing strengths and accessible entry points for change.
first_why: The recommendation to begin with teachers' existing strengths and accessible entry points is a professional-learning application of the canonical strengths-based approach, whereas the specific examples and pacing differences are narrower cases.

why: PAGE is a broader principle about selecting among many grouping formats for objectives and activities, not merely the adaptive temporary regrouping described by CANONICAL.
first_why: The candidate states the general principle of flexibly selecting and varying grouping arrangements to fit objectives, learners, and activities, which is the broader idea covered by Flexible Grouping.

why: PAGE is a narrower instructional application of Assessment for Learning, using feedback and revision within explicit-reflective NOS instruction for prospective teachers.
first_why: The candidate is a narrower application of Assessment for Learning because learners produce work against explicit criteria, receive formative feedback during instruction, and revise before judging its effectiveness.

why: PAGE describes formative assessment as a specific conference-and-feedback implementation that supports learners in evaluating their own progress.
first_why: The source directly recommends formative assessment through conferences and feedback to inform progress and support learners' self-evaluation, which is the canonical page's central practice.

why: PAGE links accumulated L2 experience and enjoyment to motivational effort, whereas CANONICAL concerns pleasurable engagement and dopamine-enhanced information processing.
first_why: The candidate directly recommends making learning pleasurable and engaging to foster intrinsic motivation and effort, which is the canonical page's central design idea.

why: PAGE presents a broader set of strategies for supporting older refugees, including affective barriers, adult-learning methods, and community goals, not merely a narrower application of connecting learning to cultural and life experiences.
first_why: The candidate's recommendations to make instruction relevant to learners' needs and connect it with refugee-community goals are a narrower population-specific application of Cultural & Life Experiences Connections.

why: PAGE describes a narrower instructional sequencing pattern—free exploration followed by organized, plan-based analysis for female learners—covered by CANONICAL's general principle of ordering tasks and supports.
first_why: This is a population-specific test of the broader sequencing principle: allowing initial exploration before explicit, organized guidance is an actionable ordering of instruction.

why: PAGE is a narrower adaptive-learning case that sequences task difficulty parameters based on learner improvement.
first_why: The recommendation is a reusable form of adaptive learning that adjusts subsequent task difficulty from learners’ observed improvement, although its control-training variables are a narrower implementation case.

why: PAGE advocates comprehensive, dimensional evaluation beyond categorical eligibility, not specifically using multiple assessment methods to measure the same goal.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower educational-assessment case for using multiple sources or approaches to understand learner functioning rather than relying on one categorical eligibility classification.

why: PAGE is a narrower expository-text application of CANONICAL's graphic-organizer principle, adding timing, vocabulary, prior-knowledge, and learner-completion guidance.
first_why: The candidate’s central recommendation—using learner-completed graphic organizers to structure and consolidate expository-text understanding—is covered by the canonical Graphic Organizers principle, while vocabulary and prior-knowledge activation are supporting components.

why: PAGE is a service-learning-specific application of CANONICAL's structured, guided reflection principle.
first_why: The candidate is a service-learning instance of structured, instructor-guided reflection, and its evidence belongs on the broader Reflection page rather than creating a separate principle.

why: PAGE describes a subject-specific, question-driven instance of guided inquiry-based learning.
first_why: The recommendation to organize a sequenced investigation around a problem-driving question is a specific implementation of inquiry-based learning, while the astronomy difficulty is only contextual evidence about learners.

why: PAGE states the same principle of choosing teaching methods based on research and evidence rather than ideology or untested theories.
first_why: The candidate directly states the canonical recommendation to choose teaching approaches from empirical evidence rather than ideology or untested theory.

why: PAGE describes a narrower computer-based-instruction case of constructive alignment, linking practice and assessment to the intended objectives.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower computer-based case of constructive alignment, linking practised responses and assessment items to the stated objectives.

why: PAGE is a narrower schoolwide curricular and environmental approach to character education, emphasizing indirect cultivation rather than separate moral instruction.

why: PAGE is a narrower instructional instance of cultivating understanding through exploration rather than directly telling learners design principles.

why: PAGE prescribes a subject-integrated, constructivist delivery model, whereas CANONICAL describes the broader aims and schoolwide practices of character education.

why: PAGE is a narrower case of authentic assessment, applying its real-practice criterion specifically to interactional speaking tasks in large-scale exams.

why: PAGE describes a specific instructional implementation of chunking by limiting study outlines to meaningful headings and key words to match learners’ processing capacity.

why: PAGE adds distinct curriculum-design and learner-power principles beyond CANONICAL’s general experiential-learning cycle.
first_why: The candidate's general experiential-learning recommendations are covered by the canonical principle, while the case-based university application is narrower and the cited benefits do not establish a distinct reusable pattern.

why: PAGE is a laboratory-specific instance of CANONICAL that applies all five cooperative-learning conditions.

why: PAGE concerns educational leadership and selection criteria for EB multimedia materials, not the canonical pattern of coordinating verbal and visual media for learning.

why: Learner Choice is a concrete design component of Autonomy, specifying how meaningful, bounded decisions can provide learners with volition and ownership.

why: PAGE is a narrower design requirement within CANONICAL's principle that the core learning activity itself must be game-like and aligned with the learning outcome.

why: PAGE concerns the distinct learning benefit of post-performance control over knowledge-of-results, not autonomy as volitional engagement and meaningful choice generally

why: PAGE is a narrower, school-based coaching implementation of CANONICAL’s broader principle that teacher professional development should be ongoing and practice-embedded.

why: PAGE is a narrower instructional-environment component of CANONICAL’s broader principle of fostering creativity through reduced evaluation and room for experimentation.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of cognitive load management that calibrates task complexity to child beginners’ capacity to preserve attention for noticing recasts.

why: PAGE is a narrower instructional-materials application of Cognitive Load Theory focused on reducing extraneous processing to support schema construction.

why: PAGE is a narrower prior-knowledge-based case of the CANONICAL worked-examples principle.

why: PAGE is a distinct optimization principle for calibrating review and new-item rates, not merely a narrower instance of CANONICAL's schedule-comparison policy
first_why: The candidate specifies a reusable spaced-review scheduling policy that calibrates review and new-item rates to maximize learning without crossing a throughput threshold, which is a narrower software implementation of the canonical Spaced Learning pattern.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of cognitive load management to older language learners through staged instruction, extra review, and wait time.
first_why: The recommendation is a reusable form of cognitive-load management: segmenting new material, pacing presentation, allowing processing time, and providing additional review for learners with greater processing demands.

why: PAGE describes mediating cultural perspectives with preservice teachers’ personal meanings, a distinct reflective process rather than cognitive disequilibrium.

why: PAGE is a distinct metacognitive and problem-solving instructional strategy within inquiry, not merely a narrower statement of what inquiry-based learning is

why: PAGE describes a narrower implementation condition for elaborative reasoning—modeling and monitoring learners’ generative answers.

why: PAGE concerns centering instruction on explaining observable phenomena through mechanistic reasoning, whereas CANONICAL concerns making successful performance processes visible through modeling.
first_why: The recommendation is a domain-specific application of modeling in which instructors make expert causal-mechanistic reasoning observable while explaining phenomena, rather than presenting phenomena only as motivational contexts.

why: PAGE describes a narrower algorithmic exercise-recommendation case of adaptive learning, selecting tasks based on mastery, difficulty, exploration, and engagement objectives.
first_why: This is a narrower application of adaptive learning: dynamically recommending exercises by balancing learner knowledge, difficulty progression, and engagement preferences.

why: PAGE is a narrower implementation of flipped learning, specifying multimedia modules as the pre-lecture exposure in introductory physics.
first_why: The recommendation is a physics-specific implementation of Flipped Learning, using monitorable multimedia modules rather than textbook reading for pre-lecture first exposure before active live-session work.

why: PAGE presents a distinct multi-criteria, culturally responsive gifted-identification principle rather than a narrower case of standardized-test fairness and bias
first_why: The recommendation directly extends standardized-test fairness to gifted identification by addressing culturally and linguistically patterned underrepresentation through multiple, less test-dependent measures.

why: PAGE is a distinct, narrower NIC-based improvement model emphasizing networked collaboration, classroom-connected work, and PDSA accountability, which CANONICAL does not capture.

why: It is a narrower articulation-and-modeling component of cognitive apprenticeship, making instructional practices and their purposes explicit to learners.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of Sequencing that uses progressively harder numbers in multiplicative tasks to target a specific anticipatory process.

why: PAGE describes embedded on-the-job technical assistance for tribal personnel, a distinct principle from ongoing teacher professional development through study teams and peer coaching.
first_why: The recommendation is a job-embedded, sustained form of professional development through coaching and collaborative work rather than one-off reports or sessions, directly supporting the canonical principle.

why: PAGE is a narrower, pronunciation-focused instance of formative assessment using instructor feedback and structured self-assessment.

why: PAGE advocates integrating simulation and observation in parallel, but does not state the canonical pattern of deliberately maintaining multiple non-reconciled model types as the intended curriculum outcome.

why: PAGE is a distinct sequencing and active-learning strategy, and puzzles need not target an existing mental model or conceptual change.

why: PAGE focuses specifically on community partners’ authority over reporting and co-authorship, a distinct knowledge-production practice not stated by CANONICAL’s broader co-creation of educational systems and practices
first_why: Community partners’ control over whether and how they participate in reporting and co-authorship is a narrower application of sharing power with communities in shaping educational knowledge and practice.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of competency-based assessment to advanced teacher certification, using demonstrated teaching performance and authentic artifacts as evidence.
first_why: The recommendation is a professional-certification application of competency-based assessment, using authentic performance evidence to judge demonstrated capability rather than knowledge tests alone.

why: PAGE focuses on sustaining autonomy support through resistance and across repeated teacher–student interactions, a distinct temporal and relational mechanism not covered by CANONICAL.
first_why: The finding directly qualifies the autonomy-support recommendation by showing that sustained, non-controlling support can foster learner initiative and engagement over time, whereas abrupt increases may backfire.

why: PAGE is a distinct counseling-language principle about how labels affect attitudes and empathy, not a narrower instructional application of CANONICAL.
first_why: Using person-first, strength-based labels is a narrower language-focused application of the canonical Strengths-based Approach, although it extends that page from naming capabilities to naming clients non-stigmatizingly.

why: PAGE describes using students as the subject of physics to connect science with everyday reality, not adapting instruction to individual learners.
first_why: The course directly instantiates the canonical personalization principle by making each learner's own body and measurements the context for understanding general physics, while the reported findings are supporting examples rather than a distinct principle.

why: PAGE is a concrete case of augmenting technology-mediated learning with complementary physical experience rather than letting simulation replace the learning process
first_why: The candidate is a narrower physics-lab case of the canonical principle that technology should augment rather than supplant learning processes, using simulation alongside the distinctive affordances of physical equipment.

why: PAGE is a workplace-instructional application of CANONICAL's broader principle of reducing avoidable linguistic barriers while preserving essential content.
first_why: The recommendation to replace jargon and officialese with audience-matched Plain English is a workplace-specific application of Accessible Vocabulary & Syntax, and its evidence belongs on that canonical page.

why: PAGE presents AI-generated podcasts as a medium-specific application of spaced learning through distributed, opportunistic listening.
first_why: The recommendation is a medium-specific application of Spaced Learning, whose canonical principle already covers distributing learning over time to support retention, while the AI-podcast and mobile-first details are narrower implementation choices.

why: PAGE is a narrower promotion-and-tenure implementation of CANONICAL’s discipline-specific RPT policies, focused on rigorously evaluating non-traditional contributions.
first_why: The candidate is a chemistry-specific application of replacing generic promotion-and-tenure engagement policies with discipline-specific review criteria and institutional support for non-traditional contributions.

why: PAGE describes the broader instructional-clarity construct and its frequency and vagueness-avoidance claims, whereas CANONICAL covers only making lesson organization and expectations explicit.
first_why: The candidate operationalizes Clear Structure through frequent signaling, framing, focusing, linking, and examples while avoiding vague or confusing organization, so its evidence belongs on that broader canonical page.

why: PAGE describes a language-focused post-task intervention in repetition activities, not the broader reflective and transfer-oriented process of debriefing.
first_why: The proposed post-task teacher-led attention to form and observed performance is a narrower language-task instance of facilitated debriefing, although the cited repetition findings only indirectly support it.

why: PAGE describes a narrower application of scaffolding—preparatory support for student question-authoring—and is well served by the canonical principle.
first_why: The candidate recommends providing instructional scaffolding before a challenging learner-generated task, which is a narrower application of the canonical scaffolding principle.

why: PAGE describes a learner-centered, schema-encoding instance of CANONICAL's broader elaborative reasoning principle.
first_why: The recommendation is a direct application of elaborative reasoning, although its cited findings support schema development and recall rather than testing learner-generated elaboration itself.

why: PAGE is a narrower middle-school multimedia-instruction case of CANONICAL's verbal–visual coordination pattern, specifically recommending narration over on-screen text to manage cognitive load.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower, middle-school science application of Multimedia Learning’s central modality and channel-selection practice, so its evidence belongs on that canonical pattern page.

why: PAGE proposes a distinct preparatory competency principle for ethical stakeholder engagement, not merely a narrower case of Community-Based Learning.
first_why: Preparing learners for ethical stakeholder engagement is a reusable implementation recommendation within Community-Based Learning, although this source presents it in a planetary-health course context.

why: PAGE is a broader instructional principle about building new knowledge from learners’ prior knowledge and experience, whereas CANONICAL focuses specifically on familiarity-driven elaborative processing and later retrieval.
first_why: The candidate directly recommends teaching new information from learners’ relevant prior knowledge, which is the central practice of this canonical principle.

why: PAGE is a narrower instructional-strategy application of CANONICAL’s broader principle of learner-generated elaboration.
first_why: Self-generated elaboration is a narrower instructional instance of Elaborative Reasoning, which already covers learners generating connections between new material and prior knowledge; the evidence should be added there rather than creating a duplicate page.

why: PAGE advocates the broader use of meaningful real-world problem solving and maker contexts for engagement and retention, not the specific instructional policy and conditions that define Problem-Based Learning.
first_why: The candidate recommends the central practice of problem-based learning—engaging learners in meaningful real-world problems—while its maker-education examples are narrower implementations of that pattern.

why: PAGE is a distinct probability-teaching claim about combining authentic contexts with randomising devices to elicit subjective reasoning, not merely a narrower application of learners’ cultural and life-experience connections.
first_why: The recommendation is a domain-specific application of connecting instruction to learners’ culturally and experientially meaningful life contexts, although the page may not fully foreground contrasting contexts to reveal reasoning.

why: PAGE centers reciprocal intercultural learning and equal contribution, which is distinct from CANONICAL's focus on previously excluded communities co-creating educational systems and practices
first_why: Reciprocal cross-cultural knowledge exchange is a narrower educational application of shared power, in which partners jointly shape content and learning rather than one side simply transmitting knowledge.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of explicit instruction in math problem-solving strategies, specifying Polya-style whole-problem instruction and a possible synthesis with translation for struggling learners.
first_why: The recommendation is a reusable form of explicit instruction in mathematical problem-solving strategies, and its verbal-problem evidence belongs on that broader page.

why: PAGE presents the three-load formulation as a specific framework for the canonical principle of managing cognitive load.
first_why: The candidate states the canonical Cognitive Load Management recommendation to differentially distribute and regulate intrinsic, extraneous, and germane processing demands, rather than proposing a narrower setting-specific application.

why: PAGE is a narrower classroom application of CANONICAL’s dialogue-based, student-centered approach, focusing on balancing teacher and student talk.

why: PAGE emphasizes immediate instrumental usefulness and authentic language contexts, whereas CANONICAL specifically concerns using learners’ own cultural and life experiences as assets.
first_why: The candidate directly recommends connecting learning materials and activities to adult learners’ familiar real-life, work, community, and instrumental contexts, which is a narrower adult-language application of this canonical principle.

why: PAGE is a remedial-reading application of CANONICAL’s strengths-based principle, adding domain-specific instructional examples.

why: PAGE states the same principle of reporting practical effect-size measures alongside statistical significance, using a narrower instructional-intervention context.

why: PAGE is a narrower mathematical case of cognitive flexibility, using shared conceptual and procedural resources to connect multiple valid solution pathways.
first_why: The recommendation is a mathematical instance of Cognitive Flexibility: representing multiple valid procedures through shared conceptual and procedural resources to help learners connect perspectives and transfer among them.

why: PAGE makes a broader theoretical claim about sociocultural SLA not prescribing normative participation, whereas CANONICAL concerns culturally responsive classroom interaction norms.

why: PAGE is a broader claim about the selective usefulness of reinforcement despite rejecting behaviorism, not a statement of the specific tiered, school-wide PBIS framework.

why: PAGE is a narrower web-based training and peer-feedback application of the canonical self-regulated-learning support principle
first_why: The recommendation is a scalable, web-based instance of explicitly teaching and prompting self-regulated planning, monitoring and action, so its evidence belongs on the canonical Self-Regulated Learning principle page.

first_why: The shared whiteboard is a digital-learning design whose value comes from specific affordances—shared annotation, a common workspace, reduced switching, and focused attention—rather than from the medium alone.

why: PAGE is a narrower test-assembly mechanism for the canonical principle of preventing bias in standardized testing conditions.

why: PAGE adds a distinct physical-siting principle—placing special classrooms near entrances and support spaces—not covered by CANONICAL’s educational-placement standard.

why: PAGE presents a psychotherapy-specific principle about adapting therapist complementarity across relationship stages, which is distinct from CANONICAL's classroom strategy of unfolding higher-order student contributions.

why: PAGE is a narrower task-design application of CANONICAL's autonomy principle, balancing structured teacher support with learner control.

why: PAGE describes a licensing-review-course application of CANONICAL's deliberate-practice principle.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower licensing-review application of deliberate practice, and its evidence belongs on the canonical Deliberate Practice principle page.

why: PAGE is a maker-education-specific application of CANONICAL's autonomy principle, focusing on meaningful student choice to foster ownership and self-efficacy.

why: PAGE describes a narrower postsecondary lecture-course application of CANONICAL's mastery-learning pattern.

why: PAGE presents a broad overview of autism spectrum disorder and its characteristics, not the narrower recommendation to prefer aided AAC over manual signs.

why: refused by the second pass: PAGE gives distinct implementation guidance about explaining spaced learning and tailoring intervals, which is not captured by CANONICAL's abstract model.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of the Motivation principle to AI policy and teacher training, specifying intervention across expectancy, value, and cost components.

why: PAGE is a narrower, context-focused application of rhetorical skill development emphasizing strategic choices within audience, situation, and institutional setting.

why: PAGE presents discovery-oriented facilitation as a narrower instance of CANONICAL's broader mediator-and-facilitator role.

why: PAGE focuses on preparing teachers to enhance each child’s learning potential rather than on the educator’s mediating role, so it is a distinct principle rather than a narrower formulation of CANONICAL.

why: PAGE combines teacher encouragement and sustained speaking practice to build self-efficacy, a distinct intervention from creating a relaxed atmosphere before communication

why: PAGE is a distinct retention-and-promotion policy whose testing options and exemptions only share assessment with CANONICAL rather than expressing a narrower competency-based assessment principle.

why: PAGE concerns trust and context-specific facilitation of reflection, which is distinct from CANONICAL’s principle of examining experience to guide action.

why: PAGE is a distinct uncertainty-aware learner-modeling principle, not a case of choosing adaptive instruction from performance evidence.

why: PAGE focuses on using real-time data collection to free time for interpretation and investigation, not on faster hypothesis exploration and solution testing.

why: PAGE makes an evidence-based case for universal multi-component programs, while CANONICAL specifies criteria for an effective classroom-wide plan.

why: PAGE is a narrower case of multimedia learning, focusing on when relevant diagrams improve learning given the processing resources and instructional conditions.

why: PAGE is a narrower application of CANONICAL's principle that technology should augment rather than replace conventional learning processes.

why: PAGE is a narrower design component of community-based learning, specifying that diversity exploration should be woven through it to support civic competence.
first_why: The recommendation is a narrower, diversity-focused component of community-based learning, and its civic-competence evidence belongs on the canonical Community-Based Learning page.

why: PAGE presents writing teachers as facilitators rather than lecturers, a narrower application of CANONICAL’s broader principle that educators should mediate learning rather than disseminate content.
